chunks: They swear by God: 'We never said this.' But they surely said words disbelieving the truth, and they turned unbelievers after having come to faith, and designed what they could not accomplish. They did it only out of vengeance for God and His Apostle had enriched them by their grace. So, if they repent it is better for them. If they turn away then God would afflict them with painful punishment in this world and the next; and none will they have on the face of the earth to protect or help them.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hypocrites' oath and their subsequent disbelief in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Banu Sulaym or specifically the hypocrite Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, highlighting the transition from outward profession to inward rejection. The 'word of disbelief' is interpreted as 'Muhammad is truthful' (or a variation thereof), which they rejected out of envy that God and the Prophet had enriched them with spiritual and material grace rather than demanding more from them. The dual punishment in this world and the hereafter underscores the immediate social and spiritual consequences of hypocrisy, with no divine protector to shield them.
